title: Homily I — Joachim and Anna, and barren grace made fruitful

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily I on the Dormition, col. 708 (PDF leaf 395)

source_text: Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννα οἱ ταύτης γεννήτορες· Ἰωακεὶμ, ὥσπερ τις προβάτων ποιμὴν, οὐχ ἧττον νέμων τοὺς λογισμοὺς, ἄγων τε κατ' ἐξουσίαν ὅποι βούλοιτο, ἢ τὰ θρέμματα. Ὑπὸ Κυρίῳ γὰρ τῷ Θεῷ ὡς πρόβατον ποιμαινόμενος, οὐδενὸς τῶν ἀρίστων ἐστέρητο. Ἄριστα δὲ λέγειν μηδεὶς οἰέσθω με, τὰ τοῖς πολλοῖς καταθύμια, πρὸς ἃ ἡ τῶν λιχνοτέρων ἀεὶ διάνοια κέχηνεν, ἃ μήτε παραμένειν πέφυκε, μήτε βελτίονα δρᾷν τὸν κεκτημένον ἐπίσταται, τὰ τοῦ παρόντος βίου τερπνὰ, ἃ μὴ δύναται βεβαίαν δύναμιν κτήσασθαι, ἀλλὰ περὶ αὐτὰ καταῤῥεῖ, καὶ αὐθωρὸν διαλύεται, εἰ καὶ τούτων πολλὴν εἶχον τὴν περιουσίαν. Ἄπαγε· οὐ πρὸς ἡμῶν ταῦτα θαυμάζειν, οὐδ' αὕτη μερὶς τῶν φοβουμένων τὸν Κύριον· ἀλλὰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ, τὰ ὄντως τοῖς εὖ φρονοῦσιν ἐφετὰ καὶ ἐράσμια, ἃ μένει διαιωνίζοντα, Θεὸν μὲν εὐφραίνοντα, καρπὸν δὲ τοῖς κεκτημένοις ἀνατέλλοντα ὥριμον, τὰς ἀρετάς φημι, αἳ τὸν καρπὸν ἐν καιρῷ αὐτῶν, τῷ αἰῶνι λέγω μέλλοντι, ζωὴν αἰώνιον δώσουσι, τοῖς γε ἀξίως φιλοπονήσασι, καὶ προσενέγκασι τὸν ἑαυτῶν πόνων ὅση δύναμις. Πόνος μὲν γὰρ προπορεύεται, ἕπεται δὲ μακαριότης αἰώνιος. Ἐντὸς Ἰωακεὶμ συνήθως τοὺς οἰκείους ἐποίμανε λογισμοὺς, ἐν τόπῳ μὲν χλόης, τῶν ἱερῶν λογίων τῇ θεωρίᾳ ἐναυλιζόμενος, ἐπὶ ὕδατος δὲ ἀναπαύσεως τῆς θείας εὐφραινόμενος χάριτος, ἐξ ἀτόπων ἐπιστρέφων, ἐπὶ δὲ τρίβους δικαιοσύνης ὁδηγῶν. Ἄννα δὲ, ἣ χάρις ἑρμηνεύεται, οὐχ ἧττον ὁμότροπος ἦν, καὶ ὁμόζυγος, πᾶσι μὲν ἀγαθοῖς κομῶσα, μυστικῷ δέ τινι λόγῳ κατεχομένη τῷ τῆς στειρώσεως ἀῤῥωστήματι. Ἐστείρευε γὰρ ὄντως ἡ χάρις, ἐν ταῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ψυχαῖς καρποφορεῖν οὐκ ἰσχύουσα· διότι πάντες ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρειώθησαν, οὐκ ἦν ὁ συνιῶν, οὐκ ἦν ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν Θεόν. Εἶτα ὁ ἀγαθὸς Θεὸς ἐπιδὼν, καὶ κατοικτειρήσας τῆς οἰκείας χειρὸς τὸ πλαστούργημα, καὶ τοῦτο βουληθεὶς ἀνασώσασθαι, λύει τὴν τῆς χάριτος στείρωσιν, τῆς Ἄννης φημὶ τῆς θεόφρονος, καὶ τίκτει παῖδα, οἷα οὐ πρότερον γέγονεν, οὐδ' αὖ πάλιν γενήσεται. Ἡ δὲ τῆς στειρώσεως λύσις ἐδήλου σαφέστατα τὴν κοσμικὴν τῶν ἀγαθῶν λυθήσεσθαι στείρωσιν, καὶ τῆς ἀποῤῥήτου μακαριότητος καρπογονεῖσθαι τὸ στέλεχος.
pass_a_gloss: Joachim and Anna her begetters (γεννήτορες); Joachim, like a shepherd (ποιμήν) of sheep, no less tending (νέμω) the thoughts (λογισμοί), and leading with authority (ἐξουσία) where he wished, than the flocks (θρέμματα). For under the Lord God as a sheep being shepherded, he was deprived (στερέω) of none of the best things (ἄριστα). Let no one think me to call best the things pleasing (καταθύμια) to the many, at which the understanding of the more greedy (λιχνότεροι) always gapes (χάσκω), which neither by nature remain (παραμένω) nor know how to make the possessor better, the delights (τερπνά) of the present life, which cannot acquire firm (βέβαιος) power, but flow down around them (καταῤῥέω) and at once (αὐθωρόν) dissolve, even if of these they/I had much abundance (περιουσία). Away (ἄπαγε)! Not for us to admire these, nor this the portion (μερίς) of those fearing the Lord; but the goods (ἀγαθά), the truly desirable (ἐφετά) and lovely (ἐράσμια) to the right-minded, which remain eternally (διαιωνίζω), gladdening God and raising up ripe (ὥριμος) fruit for the possessors, the virtues (ἀρεταί) I say, which the fruit in their season, the coming age I say, eternal life will give, to those worthily having laboured (φιλοπονέω) and offered of their own toils (πόνοι) as much as power (allowed). For toil goes before, and eternal blessedness (μακαριότης) follows. Within, Joachim habitually shepherded his own thoughts, in a place of green (χλόη), lodging (ἐναυλίζομαι) in the contemplation (θεωρία) of the sacred oracles, upon water of rest (ἀνάπαυσις) gladdened by divine grace, turning back (ἐπιστρέφω) from out-of-place things (ἄτοπα), guiding (ὁδηγέω) upon paths (τρίβοι) of righteousness. Anna, who is interpreted grace (χάρις), was no less same-mannered (ὁμότροπος) and yoke-fellow (ὁμόζυγος), abounding (κομάω) in all goods, but by some mystical (μυστικός) reason held by the infirmity (ἀῤῥώστημα) of barrenness (στείρωσις). For grace truly was barren (στειρεύω), not strong to bear fruit (καρποφορέω) in the souls of men; because all turned aside (ἐκκλίνω), together became useless (ἀχρειόομαι), there was not one understanding (συνιῶν), not one seeking out (ἐκζητῶν) God. Then the good God, looking upon (ἐπεῖδον) and pitying (κατοικτείρω) the moulded work of his own hand, and willing to save (ἀνασῴζω) it, looses (λύω) the barrenness of grace, of Anna I say, the God-minded (θεόφρων), and she bears (τίκτω) a child such as has not been before nor again will be. The loosing (λύσις) of the barrenness showed most clearly that the cosmic (κοσμική) barrenness of goods would be loosed, and that the stem (στέλεχος) of ineffable blessedness would bear fruit.
pass_b_english: Joachim and Anna were her parents. Joachim, like a shepherd of sheep, guided his thoughts no less than his flocks, leading them with authority wherever he wished. For, shepherded like a sheep under the Lord God, he lacked none of the best things (Psalm 23:1). But let no one suppose that by "the best things" I mean what pleases the many, what the minds of the greedy always gape after, things which by nature neither last nor know how to make their owner better: the pleasures of this present life, which cannot gain any lasting strength but run away and dissolve in an instant, even though they had these in great abundance. Away with them! It is not for us to admire these things, nor is this the portion of those who fear the Lord. I mean rather the good things that are truly desired and loved by those of sound mind, which endure for ever, which gladden God and bring forth ripe fruit for those who possess them: the virtues, I mean, which will yield their fruit in their season (Psalm 1:3), that is, in the age to come, the fruit of eternal life, to those at least who have laboured worthily and offered their own toils as far as they were able. For toil goes before, and eternal blessedness follows.

Within himself, as was his habit, Joachim shepherded his own thoughts: in a place of green pasture, making his dwelling in the contemplation of the sacred oracles; beside the water of rest, rejoicing in divine grace; turning them back from what was out of place, and leading them in paths of righteousness (Psalm 23:2-3).

Anna, whose name means "grace", was no less like him in her ways and was his partner in marriage, rich in every good thing, yet held fast, for some mystical reason, by the infirmity of barrenness. For grace was truly barren, having no power to bear fruit in human souls, because all had turned aside, together they had become worthless; there was none who understood, none who sought after God (Psalm 14:2-3). Then the good God looked down, and took pity on the work of his own hand, and, wishing to save it, loosed the barrenness of grace (of Anna, I mean, whose mind was set on God); and she bore a child the like of whom has never been before, nor ever will be again. The loosing of her barrenness showed most clearly that the world's barrenness of good things would be loosed, and that the stem of unspeakable blessedness would bear fruit.

choices.note: Psalm numbers converted from the Septuagint: Ps 22:1-3 LXX = Psalm 23:1-3;
Ps 13:2-3 LXX = Psalm 14:2-3 (the edition's margin gives Ps 22:2-3 and Ps 13:2-3;
Ps 23:1 is cited for "he lacked none of the best things", echoing "the Lord shepherds me and I shall lack nothing").
Psalm 14:2-3 is also quoted by Paul at Romans 3:11-12;
Psalm 1:3 ("which will yield its fruit in its season") cited for the virtues bearing fruit.
ἐξ ἀτόπων ("from what is out of place") plays on τόπῳ χλόης ("place of green pasture").
Doubtful readings: περὶ αὐτὰ καταῤῥεῖ is unclear ("flow down around them");
R. reads ἀλλ' αὐτὰ, αὐτίκα; rendered by the plain sense "run away and dissolve in an instant".
εἶχον may be "I had" or "they had"; taken as "they" (Joachim and Anna, rich in the story of the Protoevangelium), but uncertain.
τὸν ἑαυτῶν πόνων is ungrammatical as printed (likely τῶν or τὸ); rendered "offered their own toils".
ἐν ταύταις after μακαριότης αἰώνιος ("in these"); not translated.
ὁμόζυγος ("yoked together", a spouse) rendered "his partner in marriage".
The present tenses "looses ... bears" are rendered as past.
"Grace" for Anna follows the Hebrew meaning of the name, which John gives.
